proposed_fixes.title: Make settings persistence tolerate concurrent readers and writers
plan: Reproduce the exact reconnect and concurrent Settings read sequence before changing shared SettingsUtils.

Design a shared read/write protocol with bounded sharing-violation retry and atomic replacement, including reader delete sharing where replacement requires it; do not merely add FileShare.ReadWrite to in-place writes.
Serialize or coalesce MWB reconnect writes and add concurrent read/write, interrupted-write and valid-JSON preservation tests.
verification: On two physical Windows machines, keep Settings open while reconnecting repeatedly with service mode both off and on.
Verify the last successful configuration remains valid JSON and the key/layout persists after restarting both processes; verify bounded failures are reported rather than silently discarded.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The reported sharing violations fit SettingsUtils using ReadAllText and WriteAllText without a cross-process persistence protocol; in-place writes can conflict or expose partial content.

confidence.rationale: The supplied Process Monitor trace directly supports incompatible file sharing and source confirms non-atomic write behavior; atomic replacement, permissions and cross-process ordering still need a focused design.

fix_assessment.rationale: Reproduce the sharing conflict and review a shared persistence design; keep signer-rejection tracking separate.

judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the sharing conflict and review a shared persistence design; keep signer-rejection tracking separate.
evidence: The report provides a SaveSettings IOException and Process Monitor sequence with incompatible reader/writer sharing modes.
It reports lost key/layout persistence on reconnect and a higher rate in service mode; no diagnostic ZIP is supplied.
judgment.rationale: A maintainer can reproduce the supplied sequence before requesting another general report. The fix crosses shared persistence behavior and needs careful atomicity, access-control and multi-process validation.

reproduce.expected_result: Writes either succeed with valid persisted configuration or report a bounded actionable failure; no lost key/layout or partial JSON.
steps: 1. Pair the machines and change a harmless layout setting.
2. Press Ctrl+Alt+R repeatedly while Settings remains open.
3. Repeat with service mode enabled, then reboot and inspect persistence.
reproduce.title: Reproduce concurrent MWB settings persistence
prerequisites: A test pairing without production credentials
setup: Keep PowerToys Settings open on the test machines.
Record service mode and capture settings.json operations without publishing key contents.

title: [Mouse Without Borders] settings.json writes fail with sharing violation – writer and readers use incompatible FileShare modes

issue_context.summary: The report supplies a concrete settings-file sharing conflict, distinct from the separate signer-rejection reports.
initial_investigation: Read the full body and related issue 26537. SettingsUtils.GetFile uses ReadAllText and SaveSettings uses WriteAllText; SaveSettings logs exceptions without retrying in release builds.
Reader-only sharing can collide with the in-place writer. Changing the read share alone would not ensure atomic JSON or prevent competing writes.
Checked existing fork issue traces; no selected-issue design or implementation should be assumed from a similar symptom.
Reassessed the complete current issue discussion and timeline, including the latest maintainer labels. Label changes alone do not satisfy unanswered evidence requests or prove a repair.

It reports lost key/layout persistence on reconnect and a higher rate in service mode; no diagnostic ZIP is supplied.
inferences: The supplied file-sharing trace supports a persistence race, but does not independently prove every key mismatch has this cause.
